qs: In which order will the following pulley systems be most effective when attempting to lift a heavy object? (Ranked from most to least effective)

This only difference between the three pulley systems is the length of rope dangling on the left. Each rope will simply lift higher and do the same thing. Therefore, no pulley is more effective than another. They are all equally effective.
Which point is under the least amount of pressure?

This question focuses on the gravitational pull of the bar. The closer the bar is to horizontal, the higher the ‘down’ component of the gravitational force exerted on the end of the bar connected to the pointed rod. As the bar gets closer to vertical, more weight is supported by the free end of the bar (as opposed to the end fixed to the pointed bar). Therefore since B’s bar is highest, point B is under the least amount of pressure.
Which anvil is the most stable?

The greater the surface area of the part of the object against the ground, in other words, holding the weight of the object, the more stable the anvil will be. Given that C has the greatest surface area against the ground, it is the most stable.
If all gears rotate clockwise, in which direction will the rack (A) move?
Back and forth in either direction

The adjacent rack will move in the direction to the way the gears rotate. In this case, they are rotating clockwise. Therefore, the rack will move in that direction, clockwise, and thus move from left to right.
If two equally-sized forces pulled the pivoted bar in opposite directions, which of the following statements would be true?
Force A alone would keep the bar stable
Force B alone would keep the bar stable
None of the above are true

The equally-sized forces are pulling the pivoted par at different levels. This resulting force would rotate the bar, potentially horizontal. Therefore, the bar would fall, in whatever manner that may be. Thus, it is the true statement.
If a twisting force is applied to handles on a bar, in which arrangement will the bar break most easily?
A and C would require the same amount of effort
All ways would require the same amount of effort

When the bars are twisted, there will be a pressure placed on the bar, potentially resulting in a break. In bar B, the exposed middle section will have a pressure that cannot be offloaded onto something else. It is the bar most likely to break.
Is the wind stronger or weaker in the middle of the tunnel than the tunnel entrance; why?
Weaker because the entrance is bigger than the exit
Stronger because the entrance is bigger than the exit
The breeze would not feel any different
Weaker because the central part is smaller than the entrance
Stronger because the central part is smaller than the entrance
The smaller the tunnel, the more concentrated the energy of the wind becomes and thus it is stronger. As stated in the answer.
Which cog will turn the fastest?
There is no indication that a cog will somehow random turn faster than another. All cogs are interlinked which means that they will move as one and as such, all will be the same.
Which is most likely to bend if a weight is placed in the centre?
There is no indication on whether the centre is prone to bend or not. It is therefore impossible to tell whether the balance that has already bent is more likely or the straight.
There are three objects suspended on a rope. Which point of the rope has the highest tension?

The part of the rope that is suspending the biggest object is likely to have the highest tension. However, Point B is having to suspend two objects and point A all of the three objects. As such, point A will have the highest tension.
If a hammer hits a brick sitting on the floor, which point of impact is least likely to break the brick?
There would not be any difference

The middle of the brick will have the stronger resistance to breaking. Therefore, the edges, which includes both B and C will have less resistance to breaking as a point of impact. Thus, the answer is A.
At which point is the wooden beam most likely to break if it is pulled equally in the direction of the arrows?
The centre of the wooden beam is the most fragile as a point of impact. Therefore, if it was pulled in equal direction, the wooden beam at point B will be more likely to break.
If the two equal forces of air flow push from the left, which way would the turbine rotate?
If the equal forces of air flow, one pushing the turbine clockwise and one anticlockwise, the turbine would not be able to move. Therefore, it would not rotate.
Which cog has the most Rotations per Minute (RPM)?
All will have the same RPM

The question allows the only factor to be the amount of teeth the wheel has and thus its RPM. The lower the number of teeth, the more RPM the wheel will do. Given that D and A both have has the lowest number of teeth, and are the same size, they will both have the highest RPM.
How many cogs will spin clockwise?
When a cog moves in one direction, the adjacent touching cog will move the opposite. If two cogs spin anticlockwise, the other two will move in the opposite direction, clockwise.
Given that the force to all tall objects is equal, which one will be pushed over the easiest?
All methods require an equal amount of effort

The higher the force is against the tall object, the greatest the force of gravity will have in pushing the object over. Therefore, the force at point A will have the biggest gravitational pull and as such is the easiest to push over.
Once released from a compressed state, which of the four springs will reach the highest speed?

If the spring were pressed down upon, they would each increase their resulting force to return to decompression. Springs A and B have a higher free length line suggesting that they are going to be bouncing higher. This means it’ll be going faster. Since A is shorter than B, in order for it to reach the same free length line, it will need to go faster. Therefore, A will reach the highest speed.
What kind of advantage is produced by the given pulley system?
There would not be any advantage

Forces are sometimes described as a push or a pull on a given object. This pulley system uses to lift a potential object placed on it. While distance, speed and potentially velocity can be found on a pulley system, force is its primary advantage.
Given that rotating chain X is revolving clockwise, and Y anticlockwise, and each object has the same spacing between and size of its teeth, which wheel will be first to reach 4 clockwise rotations?

The wheels connecting to chain X, which is revolving clockwise, will rotate in the opposite direction. They will be going anticlockwise. The wheels connecting to chain Y will be going clockwise. Since both wheels C and D both have the same number of teeth, they will both reach 4 clockwise rotations at the same time.
Which wheel will require less effort to turn?

The longer the handle of the wheel, the less force needs to be applied to turn the wheel. The handle will have greater gravitational pull and likely greater momentum. Therefore, wheel A will require less effort to turn.
